privacy.metaDescription: Kikiboard privacy policy and cookie use.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.s1Body: The controller of data collected through kikiboard.xyz is the team behind Kikiboard. For any privacy question you can contact us at contact@kikiboard.xyz.
privacy.s2AccountBody: name, email address and authentication provider (email/password or Google OAuth), managed through Clerk.
privacy.s2ContentBody: boards, lists, tickets, subtasks, comments and attachments you create on the platform.
privacy.s2UsageBody: activity logs inside boards (actions taken, dates).
privacy.s3P3: Enable collaboration between members of a board.
privacy.s3P4: Send notifications related to user activity.
privacy.s4Intro: Kikiboard uses strictly necessary cookies for the application to work:
privacy.s4SessionBody: managed by Clerk to keep your session active securely.
privacy.s4PrefsBody: stored in localStorage (for example, acceptance of this policy). They are not sent to any server.
privacy.s4NoTrack: We do not use tracking, advertising or third-party analytics cookies.
privacy.s5Vercel: Vercel — deployment infrastructure and file storage.
privacy.s5Footer: Each of these services has its own privacy policy and security measures.
privacy.s6Body: Data is kept while the account is active. When you delete your account, all your data is permanently and irreversibly removed from our database.
privacy.s7Body: You have the right to access, rectify and delete your data. You can exercise these rights from your account settings or by contacting us at contacto@kikiboard.xyz.
privacy.s8Body: We may update this policy occasionally. For relevant changes we will notify you through the platform or by email.

howItWorks.metaDescription: From an empty board to a team that ships: the five steps of working in Kiki, explained end to end.
howItWorks.title: From an empty board to a team that ships
howItWorks.subtitle: No manual and no setup call. This is the <underline>whole flow</underline>, in the order it actually happens.

board.title: Create your board
board.body: A board is one project. Give it a name, pick a color, and if you already know your stages, name them right there while you create it.
board.b1: Starter lists on creation, or add them later
board.b2: Story points and other useful fields, already set up
board.b3: As many boards as projects you run

structure.title: Shape the work into lists and tickets
structure.body: Every column is a stage. Every card is a ticket. Move a card to the right and the work advances; drop it on a done column and it closes itself.
structure.b1: Drag and drop, or move from a menu in the list view
structure.b2: Labels, priority, dates, subtasks and attachments per ticket
structure.b3: Epics and quarters when a single board is not enough

team.title: Invite the team and share the load
team.body: Invite by email and give each person a role. Then hand out the work: one owner per ticket, an optional reviewer, and whoever else needs to be there.
team.b1: Owner, admin and member, enforced by the API
team.b2: Assignee, QA reviewer and collaborators per ticket
team.b3: Everyone involved gets notified, nobody has to chase

ai.title: Let the AI do the boring part
ai.body: The hardest part of a new project is turning what is in your head into separate tickets. Write it or say it out loud, and get the board filled for you.
ai.b1: Brain Dump: a paragraph becomes a list of tickets
ai.b2: Dictate by voice if typing gets in the way
ai.b3: Your own key, so nothing is charged to you by surprise

measure.title: Measure, close and clear
measure.body: The dashboard tells you what is overdue, what closed this week and how the load is spread. Finished work gets archived, not deleted.
measure.b2: Progress per board and per epic
measure.b3: Archive keeps history without cluttering the board

visuals.brainDumpText: We need to redo the landing, fix login on mobile and prepare the launch newsletter before Friday.

price.a: Nothing. Kiki is free to use, and the AI features run on your own provider key, so whatever you spend there you pay to them directly, not to us.

data.a: Only the people you invite to a board. Every endpoint checks membership before answering, and a ticket is only visible outside the board if you generate a share link yourself.

team.q: How many people can join a board?
team.a: There is no limit. You invite by email, and each person gets a role: admin if they should manage the board, member if they should just work on tickets.

ai.q: Do I need an AI key?
ai.a: Only for the AI features. Everything else works without it. You can bring a key from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi or any compatible endpoint, and it is stored encrypted.

languages.a: English, Spanish and Tagalog. You switch from the globe in the top bar and the choice sticks, including the dates and the activity log.

export.q: Can I connect it to my own tools?
export.a: Yes. Board activity can go to Slack or Discord through a webhook, due dates can sync to Google Calendar, and there is an MCP server so an AI assistant can work on your boards directly.

mcpOAuth.title: Connect ChatGPT to Kikiboard
mcpOAuth.description: Choose the organization or board ChatGPT may read. This connection lasts up to 30 days.
mcpOAuth.permissions: This connection can read project information and tickets. Task changes are allowed only when you explicitly enable write access.
mcpOAuth.noScopes: You need organization or board admin access to create a connection.
mcpOAuth.revoke: Revoke this connection in Settings → MCP by selecting its scope and removing the ChatGPT credential.
mcpOAuth.invalidRequest: This connection request is invalid or ChatGPT OAuth has not been configured.
mcpOAuth.writeAccess: Allow task creation, editing and archiving with reversible change history

mcpGuide.title: Connect your AI assistant
mcpGuide.intro: Choose your assistant for setup instructions. Connections stay within one organization or board. Read-only is the default; task writes require explicit permission.
mcpGuide.copyError: Could not copy. Select and copy the value manually.
mcpGuide.callbackHint: Copy the exact OAuth callback URL shown when creating your custom MCP connection in ChatGPT. Only ChatGPT callback URLs are accepted.
mcpGuide.secretOnce: Copy this secret now. It is shown only once.
mcpGuide.credentialsHint: Paste these two values into ChatGPT’s OAuth fields. This secret is different from the bearer token below. If you lose it, revoke this setup and create another.
mcpGuide.revokeHint: Revoking a setup stops its ChatGPT connections and token refreshes.
mcpGuide.createError: Could not create credentials. Check the ChatGPT callback URL and try again.
mcpGuide.tokenHint: Create and copy a scoped token below. Replace kiki_YOUR_TOKEN with that value, or securely set KIKIBOARD_TOKEN when using a shell command. Keep credentials in private configuration, never in chat prompts.
mcpGuide.test: Test with: “Use Kikiboard to list my pending tickets.”

chatgpt.intro: ChatGPT uses OAuth. Generate your own credentials here; no deployment secret is needed.
chatgpt.step1: In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins → + → Add custom MCP server. Enter the MCP URL and select OAuth.
chatgpt.step2: Copy ChatGPT’s callback URL into the field below and generate credentials. Paste the client ID and secret into ChatGPT.
chatgpt.step3: Create and install the plugin. In a Work chat, type @ and select Kikiboard.
chatgpt.step4: Sign in to Kikiboard with this same account, choose the organization or board you administer, and approve read-only or explicitly requested read/write access.

claude.intro: Claude custom connectors can send your Kikiboard bearer token as a request header.
claude.step1: Choose an organization or board below, name the connection, and create a token. Copy it when it appears.
claude.step2: In Claude, open Customize → Connectors → Add custom connector. Enter the MCP URL.
claude.step3: Select No sign in and add a request header named Authorization with value Bearer followed by a space and your token.
claude.step4: Add the connector, then enable it in your conversation using + → Connectors.

grok.intro: Use a bearer token with Grok CLI or xAI’s Remote MCP API. These steps configure Grok CLI.
grok.step1: Choose an organization or board below and create a scoped token.
grok.step2: Securely set KIKIBOARD_TOKEN in your shell environment to the token you copied.
grok.step3: Run the command below. Use grok mcp list or grok mcp doctor kikiboard to check the connection.
grok.step4: Start Grok CLI and ask it to use Kikiboard. For the xAI API, supply the MCP URL and Authorization header in a remote MCP tool.

gemini.intro: Use Gemini CLI with the Streamable HTTP configuration below. These steps are for the CLI, not the Gemini chat website.
gemini.step1: Choose an organization or board below and create a scoped token.
gemini.step2: Add the configuration below to your private ~/.gemini/settings.json, preserving your existing settings.
gemini.step3: Replace kiki_YOUR_TOKEN with your copied token. Use httpUrl for this Streamable HTTP endpoint.
gemini.step4: Restart Gemini CLI, run /mcp to check Kikiboard, and ask it to list your pending tickets.

mcpGuide.allowWrite: Request read/write access (you must also approve it during sign-in)
mcpGuide.troubleshooting: Use the public MCP URL shown here. A Vercel sign-in or deployment-protection response happens before Kikiboard checks your token. For a protected preview, an administrator can configure Vercel’s automation bypass header in clients that support it. A Kikiboard invalid-token response means you should check the copied token, expiry, revocation and selected scope.

mcpHistory.title: AI change history
mcpHistory.description: The latest 50 MCP task operations in this scope. Each batch is saved with its previous state. Reverting does not undo messages already sent to Slack or Discord.
mcpHistory.loadError: Could not load change history. Check your permissions or retry.
mcpHistory.empty: No AI task changes have been recorded here yet.
mcpHistory.previewHint: This restores the previous task fields only if nobody has edited the affected tasks since. A conflict cancels the entire revert.
mcpHistory.archiveCreated: This newly created task will be archived. Its comments, attachments and other content will be preserved.
mcpHistory.conflict: Could not revert. A task may have changed, the original list may be missing, or your permissions may have changed. Refresh the history before retrying.
